Winter a plain guide to handover calls
You can use this page

Topic: Companion Animal Travel Desk handover calls

Use this guide when you pass a pet travel case to another staff member or shift. Clear handover calls keep the traveler informed, protect the animal, and reduce missed steps at the gate, in transit, or after arrival.

Start with the essentials in plain language. Name the traveler, the pet, the route, and the current status. Keep your tone calm and direct. If the case involves special handling, say so early and make sure the next staff member knows what to watch for. When the traveler asks for a quick update, answer with the latest verified detail only.

If the pet will use the relief area at Merrowgate, share the access note with the traveler and the receiving agent. <<FACT F017>> Do not repeat the detail in different words, and do not add extra commentary around it. Keep the sentence short and let the next person move on with the case.

When a pet needs quarantine support, the handover should state that the room is ready for use and that staff should follow the usual intake check. <<FACT F029>> After that, add any observations that matter for safe care, such as feeding notes, carrier condition, or a recent change in behavior. Use a steady pace and avoid side remarks that could blur the record.

If the traveler needs a follow-up, say who will respond next and what information is still pending. The Companion Animal Travel Desk expects prompt, respectful communication, and every animal should receive patient attention from trained staff. Escalation should move in a calm, stepwise review when needed.

For more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk through the regular support channel.
